fixes.explanation: Moses says he was standing between the LORD and the people to declare to them the word of the LORD. He says the people were afraid of the fire and would not go up the mountain (Deuteronomy 5:5). So he stood in the middle and carried God's words to them. I'd call that a job with a view, and I think it took some nerve.

God says, “You shall have no other gods before Me.” This is the first command, and it comes right after He reminds them He brought them out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery. He starts with who He is and what He has done, and then He gives the command. Good work, baker.

Silent doesn't fit here. Moses says the LORD spoke these commandments in a loud voice to the whole assembly out of the fire (Deuteronomy 5:22). Nobody was straining to hear a whisper on that mountain, friend. The word God uses for Himself in this command is jealous.

Forty generations is a big number, but it's not the one God gives. He says “…a thousand generations of those who love Me and keep My commandments.” Compare that to the third and fourth generations He just mentioned, and the difference is huge. My whole family is six cookie cutter kids and a mustache, so a thousand generations is a number I can barely picture. The number to hold on to is a thousand, baker.

Trade is a fair-sounding guess, but it's not the word. God says, “You shall not steal.” That's about taking what belongs to someone else. I came out of the bottom of a bakery's last bin with a 25 cent sticker on me, and the Millers paid for me. Paying is a different thing from stealing.
